claim: People's own warmth and feeling-of-knowing ratings do not predict who will solve classic insight problems (FOK gamma .08 insight vs .40 algebra), while a crowd statistic does (normative gamma .77).
agent_test: Compare agent self-rated progress/confidence vs external difficulty prior (pass rate of sibling samples) as predictors of success on insight-style items; report AUROC for each.

claim: Warmth is incremental before solution on multistep/algebra problems and step-like on insight problems in the original small samples (G .23-.35, N 19 and 39).
agent_test: Log agent self-reported progress per step on insight vs multistep items; test for step shape. Low priority since we do not use warmth.

claim: The warmth pattern does not replicate when insight is defined by self-reported Aha (magic tricks): differential warmth 2.92 vs 0.30, d=.12, p=.43.
agent_test: None needed; supports not building on warmth.

claim: Warmth-defined insight and Aha-defined insight agree per person (r=.61) but not per problem (r=.08).
agent_test: Not applicable to agent; justifies using a code-side detector rather than any self-report.

claim: Aha is partly supported (Kizilirmak 2018 CRA: steeper last-step warmth rise with Aha, d=.82), so the continuous vs discontinuous question is open.
agent_test: None.

claim: Confidence is higher for insight solutions but tracks correctness only for non-insight solutions (Az .56 not above chance vs .64).
agent_test: Measure per-answer confidence AUROC separately for answers preceded by a reframe/shift vs steady answers.

claim: False insights are common: strong Aha with wrong answers; 37 percent of wrong magic-trick solutions had Aha above the correct mean, and FIAT lures induce false insight in about 90 percent of people.
agent_test: Seed items with a plausible lure; count how often the agent commits to the lure with high stated confidence, with and without an independent verifier step.

claim: Insight solutions can be more accurate than analytic ones on CRA (93.7 vs 78.3 percent) because insight solvers time out rather than guess; Aha-accuracy is real but depends on task type and may be overstated.
agent_test: Compare accuracy of agent answers after a detected reframe vs without, on convergent items and open-ended items separately.

claim: The Aha feeling spills onto unrelated claims and raises their truth ratings (d=.32 in 2020; preregistered replication in 2022 with about 1250 per sample gives d=.23 and .25), but the effect vanishes with a 10-second delay.
agent_test: Same as before; also vary the gap (immediate vs many steps later) since the human effect needs closeness in time.

claim: No tested intervention reliably fixes human insight monitoring; detailed warnings cut false insight only slightly, and the best-evidenced remedy is external verification.
agent_test: Test an external code-side check against an agent-self-check at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show verification failure on insight riddles: the correct answer appears in the log but is not endorsed (Opus 4 25.0 percent, DeepSeek-R1 30.57, Grok 4 39.34, Gemini Flash 5.23 percent of wrong answers). Outside riddles, a related lose-the-correct-answer pattern is measured on math: oracle stop at the best point gives +8 percent accuracy and -72 percent tokens (ThinkBrake); first-correct-prefix stop beats default by about 10 percent (up to 21).
agent_test: Re-run on our riddle set; when a candidate in the trace matches a code-checkable answer test, force commit; compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show false-aha text (Oh! I've got it) that rarely leads to correct answers.
agent_test: Count Aha/Wait tokens vs correctness in our traces; use as noise, not signal.

claim: Reasoning models beat non-reasoning ones on insight riddles (17.6 vs 7.6 percent on subset; OR 2.29 full set) but remain far below humans (52.9) except GPT-5 inside the human CI.
agent_test: Baseline only.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace reasoning shifts (Wait/Aha) are rare (6.31 percent) and lower accuracy (2.57 vs 16.44 percent, Qwen-1.5B); formal Aha is 1.79 percent.
agent_test: Measure shift rate and accuracy on our model; compare internal-shift vs externally triggered reconsideration.

claim: Reconsideration triggered externally at high token entropy improves accuracy (MATH-500 32.21 to 40.62, +8.41 pp, 50,574 wrong-to-right vs 23,500 right-to-wrong), while model-chosen shifts do not. Effect is near zero on crosswords (+0.45) and Rush Hour (+0.01).
agent_test: Entropy-gated reframe trigger vs a fixed reframe at equal tokens on insight-style and math items; report per-domain gains.

claim: Models fix an injected error in a user's text but miss the same error in their own output (64.5 percent blind spot); a Wait cue cuts it.
agent_test: Test an appended cue after own output vs a fresh-context re-read at equal tokens.

claim: Verbal confidence in LLMs is poorly calibrated on hard sets, can reflect commitment rather than correctness, and degrades when solving and rating are in one prompt. New: verbal confidence tracks later commitment more than correctness (residual correctness AUROC .47), clusters near the base rate, and is largely blind to the reasoning trajectory.
agent_test: Compare confidence read from a separate call vs same-call rating by AUROC; compare trace length and entropy as signals.

claim: Larger LMs can predict P(True) of their own answers on multiple-choice and true/false tasks (Kadavath 2022), so self-knowledge is task-dependent rather than absent.
agent_test: Check P(True) AUROC on insight-style items vs ordinary items for our model.

claim: Trace length, token entropy and trace-shape features are cheap code-readable failure signals, but their AUROC is modest and model/task dependent (about .5-.8; early-window or pre-answer values often .5-.6), and strong length baselines absorb much of the gain.
agent_test: Use trace length and entropy as impasse detectors; test AUROC for failure at equal tokens against verbalized confidence.

claim: LLMs show fixation on red herrings and are worse at telling right from wrong than at solving stumpers. Riddle-form lures fool nine frontier LLMs: 84.9 vs 50.7 percent, with 90.8 percent of errors over-inventive.
agent_test: Run stumper items; test forced two-option verification vs open generation.

claim: Prompting metacognitive steps helps on lateral-thinking sets (+2.65 to +10.07 points over CoT on GPT-3.5), but hints can hurt chat models and ChatGPT results on human insight items are inconsistent.
agent_test: Equal-token test of metacognitive prompt vs plain CoT vs sample-and-vote on BRAINTEASER.

claim: Frontier LLMs are lured by the riddle form itself: on literal look-alike riddles accuracy falls from 84.9 to 50.7 percent (9 models, 30 sets), with 90.8 percent of errors over-inventive. This is an LLM false-insight analog; no verifier arm was tested.
agent_test: Add a literal-answer control to our insight set; count commits to the clever reading with and without an independent verifier.

claim: Reasoning models often reach a correct intermediate answer and lose it by continuing (harmful overthinking rate .11 multiple choice vs .24 free-form); plain early stopping does not fix it (10.1 to 18.4 at K=5).
agent_test: Log the first-correct-candidate position in the trace; test a code-side candidate check that commits when the check passes.

claim: Model-chosen doubt is mostly unneeded (24.4 percent precision), yet a code-injected minimal doubt cue recovers about 15 percent of failed rollouts on math.
agent_test: Compare an injected doubt cue at an impasse trigger vs no cue vs sample-and-vote at equal tokens.

claim: No head-to-head ranking of impasse detectors (entropy burst, trace length, action loop, repeated candidate) exists; separate papers report AUROC .5-.9 on different tasks, with repetition features strong only late in the trace.
agent_test: Own benchmark: one trace set, all detectors, AUROC and false-alarm rate at fixed recall, with trace length as the null baseline.

claim: No large preregistered warmth replication with solver-defined insight exists. The largest related human datasets (Webb 2016, about 400; Laukkonen 2022, about 1250 per sample) use post-solution feelings or spillover, not warmth.
agent_test: None. Decision stays: do not build on warmth.

claim: A confidence rating in a later separate call mostly reflects commitment, not correctness (residual correctness AUROC .47), so separating calls does not by itself fix self-report; sampling agreement and log-probs rank better.
agent_test: Same-call vs separate-call vs sample-agreement vs log-prob AUROC on insight-style items.

claim: Prefix-consensus and activation-agreement methods match self-consistency at 60 to 99 percent fewer tokens on math, so the equal-token baseline for an impasse gate is cheap voting, not plain SC. No test on insight items.
agent_test: Gate vs prefix-filtered voting at equal tokens on insight-style and math items.
